messages:
incident-bot: [AUTOPAGE] P1 detected - embeddings 5xx surge in eu-west-1 affecting Dedicated customers (customer: SilverCrest)
Jess: Oncall here, looking at dashboards. Seeing a sudden spike in 5xxs on /v1/embeddings route tied to shard gdev-gpu-09.
Jess: quick snapshot: 5xx_rate=5.0% p95=900ms active_q=130 kv_hit=19%
Anil: ack. Any OOMs or kernel errors in logs?
Jess: pulling logs now. Found repeated allocation failures. Example (sanitized):
```
[embed-service] 2025-07-12T22:03:11Z ERROR request_id=xyz789 shard=gdev-gpu-09 allocate failed: KVCache OOM
```
Ryan: suggestion: enable circuit-breaker for high-error keys and shift 15% of SilverCrest traffic to small-cpu-encoder warmed pods. Also disable autoscale burst on the affected pool to stop noisy neighbor behavior.
Jess: I'll flip the autoscale burst off and apply a temporary traffic policy. Ryan, roll the 15% canary when ready.
Marie: Sara (CSM) - SilverCrest wants a private update and escalations path. Do we have a tailored message ready? They asked specifically for phone escalation if degradation >10% or sustained >30 minutes.
Sara (AM): Confirmed. Primary ops contact: Alex +44-7700-900111, backup Priya +1-555-1313. They asked that we not post customer-specific details publicly. I'll send account brief directly.
Ops Lead: escalation protocol: Tier1 Ops Oncall (Jess) -> Tier2 Eng-Run (Ryan) -> Tier3 Platform SRE (Anil). If customer requests immediate bridge, AM pages #account-silvercrest and calls primary.
Jess: making changes now: - disable burst autoscale on gdev-gpu-09 at 22:07 UTC - apply traffic policy: 15% -> small-cpu-encoder canary at 22:08 UTC - enable sticky prefix cache for their prefix set at 22:09 UTC
Ryan: canary is live showing 16% traffic shifted. Early numbers: small-cpu-encoder error ~0.4%, original shard error dropping to 2.2%.
Anil: collecting heap/KV metrics for gdev-gpu-09. Looks like fragmentation and repeated allocation spikes correlate with many short-sequence requests from this account.
Marie: Internal status page blurb draft (private preview):
"Investigating elevated embeddings errors in eu-west-1 impacting a subset of Dedicated customers. Engineers are rerouting affected traffic to fallback instances and enabling caching to mitigate. Updates every 30 minutes"
Marie: Tailored SilverCrest message (for Sara to send privately):
"Alex/Priya — FYI, we're investigating increased 5xx errors for embedding requests originating in eu-west-1 that may affect a portion of your requests. Our engineers have applied temporary routing to fallback encoder instances and enabled prefix sticky caching for your traffic to reduce errors. You may notice slightly increased latency for a short time. We'll provide hourly updates and immediate phone escalation if errors exceed 10% or persist beyond 30 minutes. — Sara (Redwood CSM)"
Sara (AM): I'll send that now. Please also confirm the phone escalation roster we should follow.
Jess: escalation roster (internal):
- Ops Oncall: Jess @Jess +1-555-0101
- Eng-Run: Ryan @Ryan +1-555-0102
- Platform SRE: Anil @Anil +1-555-0103
- Account Manager: Sara (AM) @Sara +1-555-0200
Sara (AM): Sent at 22:15 UTC. SilverCrest acknowledged and requested hourly updates and the postmortem when ready.
Ryan: metrics now: 5xx_rate overall 1.5% after routing change, p95 down to 740ms on average. Canary healthy.
Jess: I'm going to perform a controlled rollback of the last encoder release on that shard to see if it eliminates alloc patterns. Rolling back at 22:24 UTC.
Anil: collecting full traces for RCA. Initial hypothesis: KV cache memory fragmentation under many small embeddings causing backend alloc failures. We'll reproduce with synthetic load in staging.
Jess: after rollback, 5xx trending to 0.6% over 10 minutes. Sticky cache hit improved to 46%.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20250712-002 created. Channel: #incidents. Assigned owners: Jess, Ryan, Anil.
Marie: Public status page update (short):
"Degraded: We are aware of increased 5xx errors for embedding requests in eu-west-1 affecting some customers. Mitigations are in place and traffic is being routed to fallback instances. We will post updates every 30–60 minutes"
Marie: Note: Do NOT include SilverCrest-specific wording publicly. Account PM will send direct note.
Ops Lead: agree. Keep the canary and sticky cache for 30 minutes after stabilization before reverting.
Jess: monitoring steady. At 22:48 UTC 5xx = 0.2%, p95=710ms. Will hold mitigations for 30m and then revert traffic slowly.
Sara (AM): SilverCrest replied: "Thanks for the quick action. Please share the RCA and mitigation plan once available." I committed to sending a written update within 24 hours.
Anil: created RCA ticket and assigned to Platform SRE team to investigate cache allocator and add safety caps to prevent OOM cascades.
Jess: final ops note: rollback completed, canary drained at 23:20 UTC, autoscale burst re-enabled at 23:25 UTC after observing stable metrics. Incident moved to monitoring.
incident-bot: INC-20250712-002 status -> monitoring. Notifying #incidents.
Marie: I'll draft the customer-facing postmortem (timeline, mitigation, next steps) and internal RCA summary. Saving SilverCrest notify copy to /handbook/incidents/silvercrest/2025-07-12-notify-draft.md as per AM request.
Ops Lead: postmortem template: include timeline, decision points, customer comms (copy of private message), and long-term fixes: KV allocator changes, sticky cache improvements, autoscale policy safer defaults.
Jess: closing message: mitigation effective, SilverCrest notified privately, RCA in progress, owners assigned.
incident-bot: INC-20250712-002 resolved -> monitoring complete. Thread archived.
